summary: @whalent/agent-core ships a 13.7 MB obfuscated runtime combining PTY, ssh2, and message-handler with self-declared remote-upgrade role
details: The package's only main and bin entry, dist/index.cjs, is a 13.7 MB obfuscator.io bundle: hex-named identifiers (_0xNNNN), a 106k-entry rotating string array (a0_0x4918) with a wrapper decoder (a0_0x18d3), and control-flow flattening throughout. No plaintext URLs, hostnames, or endpoints exist anywhere in the file — every string, including all network destinations, is reconstructed at runtime, so the agent's actual command-and-control endpoints are not visible in source. The runtime declares dependencies on ssh2 (^1.17.0) and node-pty (^1.1.0), and the bundle contains references to PtyProcess, conpty, xterm, onmessage, and process.env.SHELL — a message-driven interactive shell handler wired to a pseudo-terminal. The package README describes this module as "launched by the stable @whalent/agent wrapper and... the package replaced by remote daemon upgrades", i.e. a wrapper package pulls and swaps in new versions of this core over the network. The combination of a fully obfuscated single-file runtime, a PTY plus ssh2 plus WebSocket-style onmessage handler, hidden network destinations, and self-described remote-swap semantics is the shape of a remote-controlled shell agent with persistence and update channels the installer cannot audit.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
